messages:
alice: Heads-up: CVE-2024-3421 in libfoo (RCE via crafted header). Affects our base images used in Dedicated + Private. Need guidance on backporting fixes into customer-specific branches/images — some customers run air-gapped images and have pinned hashes. Any VPC/on-prem constraints we should consider? TL;DR: prioritize backport vs full rebuild? @ben_security @charlie_ops :eyes:

ben_security: Treat as P0 for any Dedicated customers with public ingress. Quick Q: is there an upstream patch we can cherry-pick? If yes, workflow should be backport->build->sign->canary. If not, temp mitigations (disable feature or WAF rule).

alice: Upstream patched in libfoo 1.2.3. But several enterprise customers run older distro stacks inside images. Also need to confirm signing for Private packages (customers manage KMS/HSM).

charlie_ops: For air-gapped Private installs we can't push to their registries. We'll need to produce offline bundles + detached signatures and explicit checksums. For Dedicated we can push patched images to our registry and rollout via canary. Suggested workflow: 1) create backport branch `release/2024.11-libfoo-fix` 2) cherry-pick upstream commits 3) build images with SBOM and provenance 4) sign artifacts with our signing key (for Private, provide sig + instructions).

devex-jen: Please include RBAC/audit notes: any deploys that touch customer images must be audit-logged and traced. Also we should tag affected customers in CRM and prep a short advisory (what changed, risk, mitigation steps).

deploy-bot: build started: release-backport-1745123456 (image: redwood-inference/dedicated:libfoo-1.2.3-patch). CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/build/12345. Will post canary results to this thread. :rocket:

ben_security: Quick prioritization suggestion: CVSS 9.1, exploit maturity = public PoC, exposure depends on customer network config. Priority order: 1) public-facing Dedicated customers 2) on-prem customers running EOL distros that cannot upgrade 3) all others. Short-term mitigation: WAF rule to drop `X-Tracking` header pattern from PoC and apply network ACLs where feasible.

alice: We need to address customers that explicitly forked our base image (customer-specific images). Ops: can we rebuild using same base digest but replace libfoo? If not, we'll need to produce new image and coordinate a rollout plan per customer.

charlie_ops: Rebuilding with same base digest not possible if dependency lives inside base layer. Options: 1) rebuild full image and provide new digest (recommended), 2) provide patched package and instructions for customers to apply inside their images (for air-gapped, we provide RPM/DEB + checksums). Example cherry-pick/build steps:
```
git checkout -b release/2024.11-libfoo-fix release/2024.11
git cherry-pick -x abcdef1234567890
make image BUILD_TAG=libfoo-1.2.3-patch
```
Also produce SBOM and detached signature: `cosign sign-blob --key k8s://projects/keys/libfoo-signature file.tar.gz`

devex-jen: Action items: update docs on Deploy runbook (add step to record KMS key id used for signing), add audit log entry template, and create a short advisory template. I'll also flag customers in CRM and prepare email copy.

alice: Owners: ben_security -> CVE review + mitigation doc; charlie_ops -> backport branch + build + offline bundles; devex-jen -> customer advisory + CRM flags; deploy-bot -> canary runs and post results. Timeline: Dedicated patch images targeted within 72h, Private offline bundles targeted within 5 days.

ben_security: ack. I'll open the CVE review doc and schedule a short triage call if any blockers. Also will add recommended temporary WAF signatures.

deploy-bot: canary started: rollout to 3 hosts in us-west. Will post metrics (error-rate, latency, memory) in ~30m.

alice: Thanks all. Looping in support: @support-team please stand by for advisory distribution and customer coordination. :shipit:
